items.article: Adam Mockler has revealed what set Scott Jennings off during their viral on-air clash. The 23-year-old commentator who sparked a viral outburst from CNN’s token MAGA host says it should disqualify him from being President Donald Trump’s next press secretary. Adam Mockler tells The Daily Beast Podcast that Scott Jennings lost control during the outburst, which came as part of a desperate defense of Trump’s never-ending war with Iran. “He lost control of himself, and it’s embarrassing,” Mockler said. “I can’t picture him standing up there as the press secretary in these combative environments.” He continued, “I mean, him getting personal with me on the panel is just so below what an experienced anchor should do. I’ve been doing CNN hits for one year. He’s been doing it for a decade. The fact that he lost his s--t due to the Iran war is very indicative of how thin-skinned he is.” Jennings, 48, blew up at Mockler during an April panel on NewsNight with Abby Phillip , after Mockler pressed him on what political concessions the U.S. secured from Iran during Trump’s war, which was still only eight weeks old at the time. Mockler told host Joanna Coles he thought Jennings had gotten “increasingly frustrated” after backing himself into an “indefensible position” by defending a war Trump had initially claimed would be over within five weeks.

items.article: Maya Jama, Michael Sheen and Bella Ramsey are among this year's celebrities taking part in the show. The Celebrity Traitors is back for a second series, and viewers will see the likes of Michael Sheen, Jerry Hall, Richard E Grant and Amol Rajan at the round table along with Bella Ramsey, Leigh-Anne Pinnock, Maya Jama and King Kenny. There are 21 celebrities taking part in total - two more than last year - and there will be an extra episode after the huge popularity of last year's series. The extended 75-minute debut episode starts at 20:00 BST on Thursday, with Claudia Winkleman again hosting the murderous game. Viewers can expect some fresh ideas, and executive producer Sarah Fay said they "always want to push the envelope" with the show's elaborate tasks. "We're always trying to evolve existing ideas to bring them into a new life or coming up with different cultural references," she told the show's press launch. The celebrities will be playing for a £100,000 cash prize for charity.

items.article: Trump is sending $500 checks to nearly a million Americans insured under the ACA ahead of the midterms, with a letter promoting his healthcare record. President Donald Trump is sending $500 checks to nearly a million Americans this week, along with a letter promoting his record on healthcare. The US Treasury is releasing the checks to over 950,000 Americans across 30 states who were enrolled in Affordable Care Act health insurance plans, an administration official said. The letter from the president was set to be mailed out to recipients on Thursday. "For years, the Biden Administration overcharged you to fund the operation of HealthCare.gov. That money belongs to hard-working Americans, not the Government, and now, I am returning it to you!" Trump begins the letter. Trump previously announced plans to send out the Affordable Care Act refund checks in early September, saying the Biden administration had overcharged enrollees and "accumulated a significant surplus of funds that were not used to benefit the Americans who paid these higher premiums." The payments are coming about a month before Americans head to the polls for the midterm elections . They're also part of a trend of Trump promising cash payments in his second term. The president said this month he would send every American adult a $5,000 " Trump dividend " if Republicans maintained control of the House and Senate in November. items.text: What you need to know about the new gun control laws Newsom signed
items.article: Over the weekend Gov. Gavin Newsom signed ten new gun safety bills into law, many aimed at strengthening gun safety protections. For California gun owners who may not have heard, over the weekend Gov. Gavin Newsom signed ten new gun safety bills into law , many aimed at strengthening gun safety protections and improving firearm training standards. This comprehensive gun safety package is the latest move in Newsom and other state leaders' attempts to have California lead on gun safety by improving enforcement of existing firearm prohibitions, expanding safe-storage tools, supporting survivors and communities, and addressing emerging threats from new technologies. However, gun-rights activist organizations like the National Rifle Association of America argue that several of the bills signed into law are ultimately an "attack on law-abiding gun owners." Perhaps the most contentious law signed into law was Senate Bill 948 , which will require California residents who purchase a new firearm to take a four-hour safety class and a live-fire shooting exam to obtain a firearm safety certificate. The law takes effect in January 2029. Additionally, starting in January 2028, folks moving to California from other states will need to obtain a firearm safety certificate within 180 days of arriving, or they will receive a misdemeanor. The bill's author, Jesse Arreguín (D-Berkeley), says its approval builds on California's strong "common-sense laws" and creates "consistent safety standards"
